notes: A planned chain as the chain planner publishes one: a definition and the prose companion beside it, under one stem. The suite copies both into a scratch workspace staged the way the umbrella-runtime test stages one - two members under projects/, then umbrella init - and runs the workspace runtime's own validate over the pair, expecting ok true and exactly one warning, the freshly scaffolded manifest's reserved-key:routing.tiers advisory, which is the workspace's and not the chain's. The pair holds only constructs the grammar has: one inline node declaring a bool value output, one gate with one continue and one stop, two dispatching nodes into two declared members with a provider each, one guarded node whose bool comes from inside its own needs closure, and one inline close-out. No reserved key appears anywhere, including as a node id. docs-refresh.plan.md is the third file the planner publishes, the reasoning a dry-run reviewer reads; the suite pins its four required headings, in order, because the skill requires them and nothing else proves them. docs-refresh.md and docs-refresh.plan.md carry schema null because a prose companion is judged by the graph checker's heading-equality lint and a plan file by the suite's heading pin, not by a schema. expect is absent on purpose: the corpus-wide consumer of expect.warnings is hard-wired to the reserved-key fixture, so a warning expectation declared here would assert nothing - the expectation is asserted in the suite instead.
